card.name: Inside co-administration and interaction phrases
card.fires_on: Words in drug-interaction sentences just before or inside a second drug name, such as partway through coadministration or concomitant, or the word be after 'should'. It also fires on the end of a drug name after 'concomitant use of'.

modes.label: Inside coadministration words
modes.description: Partway through coadminister, coadministration or concomitantly, in interaction text.
modes.example: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Tamoxifen Coad<<min>>istration of letrozole and tamox

modes.label: Late in a paired drug name
modes.description: Final piece of a drug name in a pair such as imipenem and cilastatin or cyclosporine.
modes.example: id Concomitant administration of Imipenem and Cilast<<atin>> for Injection (I.V.) and prob

modes.label: Be after should
modes.description: The word be after 'should' in a sentence about giving drugs together or timing.
modes.example: Concomitant administration with fluorouracil should<< be>> avoided.

card.plain: It marks the middle of drug-interaction sentences about giving two medicines together.
